title: Greet the user
description: Write a script that asks the user for their name with the exact prompt `"What is your name? "`, then prints a greeting in the exact form `"Hello, <name>!"`.
examples:
What is your name? Ana
Hello, Ana!
hints: You'll need to read a line of text from the user before you can greet them.
The built-in `input()` function displays a prompt and returns whatever the user typed as a string.
Call `input('What is your name? ')` and store the result, then print it with an f-string like `f'Hello, {name}!'` matching the wording exactly.
expected_behavior: Prompts for the user's name and prints a greeting containing it, followed by an exclamation mark.

hidden_tests.expected_stdout: What is your name? Hello, Ana!
hidden_tests.label: name Ana

hidden_tests.expected_stdout: What is your name? Hello, Bo!
hidden_tests.label: name Bo

explanation: `input()` prints its argument as a prompt without a newline, then blocks until the user types a line and presses enter, returning that line as a string. Embedding it in an f-string builds the greeting with the entered name.
